title: Shannon bound for small circuits
statement: For every natural number $n$, consider the set of Boolean functions on $n$ inputs computable by a well-formed, fan-in-at-most-two acyclic circuit with AND, OR, and NOT gates, whose gates read only earlier vertices and whose output is a circuit vertex, and whose size (number of inputs plus gates) is at most $\left\lfloor 2^n/(10n)\right\rfloor$. Under the uniform distribution on all Boolean functions on $n$ inputs, the probability of choosing a function in this set is at most $2^{-2^n/10}$.
hypotheses_covered: The circuit has $n$ inputs and gates ordered so each gate reads only earlier vertices
The output is a circuit vertex
Each gate has distinct arguments, and every NOT gate has exactly one argument
Every gate has at most two arguments
Circuit size, the number of inputs plus gates, is at most the natural-number quotient $2^n/(10n)$
